If at any time the employee concerned was indisputably an employee of the establishment and subsequently it is so disputed, such a question is an incidental question arising under Section 32 of the Act. Even the case pleaded by the respondent-Union itself is that the appellant establishment had never recognised the workmen mentioned in Exhibit "A" as its employees and throughout treated these persons as the employees of the second respondent. If that dispute existed throughout, we think, the Labour Court or the Industrial Court under the Act is not the appropriate Court to decide such question, as held by this Court in General Labour Union (Red. Flag), Bombay v. Ahmedabad Mfg. and Calico Printing Co. Ltd., 1995 Supp (1) SCC 175 (supra), which view was reiterated by us in Vividh Kamgar Sabha v. Kalyani Steels Ltd., 2001 (1) Cur LR 532 (SC). 10. Next decision relied upon by Shri Singhvi is the Central Bank of India Ltd. v. P.S. Rajagopalan, (1964) 3 SCR 140 to contend that even in cases arising under Section 33-C (2) of the Industrial Disputes Act the scope, though very limited, certain incidental questions can be gone into like a claim for special allowance for operating adding machine which may not be based on the Sastry Award made under the provisions of Chapter V- A. The learned counsel pointed out that in the event we were to hold that it is only in clear cases or undisputed cases the Labour Court or the Industrial Tribunal under the Act can examine the complaints made thereunder, the whole provisions would be rendered otiose and in each of those cases provisions of the Bombay Industrial Regulations Act, 1946 or the Industrial Disputes Act will have to be invoked. We are afraid that this argument cannot be sustained for the fact that even in respect of claims arising under Section 33-C(2) appropriate dispute can be raised in terms of Section 10 of the Industrial Disputes Act and that has not been the position in the present case. Nor can we say that even in cases where employer- employee relationship is undisputed or indisputably referring to the history of relationship between the parties, dispute can be settied and not in a case of the present nature where it is clear that the workmen are working under a contract. But it is only a veil and that will have to be lifted to establish the relationship between the parties. That exercise, we are afraid, can also be done by the Industrial Tribunal under the Bombay Industiral Relations Act, 1946 or under the Industrial Disputes Act. Therefore, we are afraid that the contention advanced very ably by Shri Singhvi on behalf of the respondents cannot be accepted. Therefore, we hold hat the High Court went far beyond the scope of the provisions of the Act and did not correctly understand the decisions of this Court in Gujarat Electricity Board, Thermal Power Station, Ukai, Gujarat v. Hind Mazdoor Sabha, 1995 Lab IC 2207 (supra) and General Labour Union (Red. Flag), Bombay v. Ahmedabad Mfg. and Calico Printing Co. Ld. 1995 Supp (1) SCC 175 (supra). The correct interpretation of these decisions will lead to the result, which we have stated in the course of this order." In the case of Vividh Kamgar Sabha v. Kalyani Steel Limited, 2001 (1) Cur LR 532, the view of the Supreme Court is the same that if the employer- employee relationship is undisputed or indisputable then the complaint under MRTU & PULP Act is maintainable.  11. Conversely when the relationship of employer-employee is disputed or is questionable, the Court constituted under the MRTU & PULP Act has no jurisdiction to entertain the complaint unless the status of relationship of employer and employee is first determined in the proceedings under the BIR Act, 1946 or the Industrial Disputes Act. Logically, therefore in the complaint filed under the MRTU & PULP Act, the Court constituted thereunder is not competent to adjudicate the relationship of employer-employee.  12. In the case in hand the relationship of employer-employee has been called in question by the first appellant. The thing then remained to be seen by the Industrial Court was to find out whether the relationship of employer- employee is questionable. What is significant to be noticed is that the day on which the interim order came to be passed, the Industrial Court also passed an order direction the first appellant to produce muster roll and wage registers from 1990 till March, 2004 of its employees and also produce the leave records maintained by the first appellant for the period 1990 until March, 2004 of its employees. That suggests that the Industrial Court was not sure whether relationship of employer-employee was capable of being questioned by the first appellant. The Industrial Court constituted under the MRTU & PULP Act is not clothed with the Jurisdiction to adjudicate the employer-employee relationship nor there is anything like prima facie consideration of relationship of employer-employee in the complaint under the said Act. In our considered view since the jurisdiction of the Industrial Court in passing the interim order under Section 30(2) is founded upon the consideration of the aspect whether the complaint under Section 28 is entertainable and that depends on the relationship of employer-employee in a case like this where such relationship is called in question, the Industrial Court was required to consider the aspect as to whether the employer-employee relationship is unquestionable on the basis of the pleadings of the parties and the available material and then proceed with consideration of prayer for interim relief if it was of the view that employer-employee relationship was unquestionably and not in the manner he did prima facie overrated the objection of the first appellant, granted interim relief and then decided to hold the enquiry into relationship of employer-employee by calling for record from first appellant. This aspect has been overlooked by the learned single Judge.  13. We accordingly, set aside the order of the learned single Judge dated July 13, 2004 and the order of the learned Industrial Court, Mumbai dated June 1, 2004 (Exhibit `L' and `M'). The application made by the complainants under Section 30(2) of the MRTU & PULP Act for interim relief is restored to the file of the Industrial Court, Mumbai for fresh consideration in the light of the observations made hereinabove. The parties are directed to produce entire material in support of their rival case within two weeks from today, if not produced so far. We clarify that it would be open to the Industrial Court to call for further material from the appellants if the said Court finds that necessary.  14. The Industrial Court is directed to hear and decide the application for interim relief as early as possible and preferably within four weeks from the date of receipt of this order.  15. We direct the appellants to maintain the status-quo in respect of the plant and machinery as well as the complainants as obtaining today until the disposal of application under Section 30(2).  16. The Industrial Court shall obviously keep in mind our observations made hereinabove and the judgments of the Supreme Court in the case of Cipla Limited 2001 Lab IC 1108 (supra) and Kalyani Steels Limited 2001 Lab IC 499 (supra) and the Division Bench judgment of this Court in the case of Hindustan Coca Cola Bottling Pvt. Ltd. v. Bhartiya Kamgar Sena, 2001 (3) Cur LR 1025.  No costs.  Order accordingly.
summary: Maharashtra Recognition of Trade Unions and Prevention of Unfair Labour Practices Act, 1971, Sections 28 and 30(2) - Appellants - Complainants - The complainants have been granted interim relief, restraining the appellants from terminating their services until the disposal of the complaint. However, the question as to whether the ‘employer-employee' relationship was unquestionable was not considered. An application has been made for the grant of interim relief restored, and the order of the single judge has been set aside. [Para 12]

text: Arjit Pasayat, J. - Leave granted.  2. The Union of India questions legality of judgment rendered by Division Bench of the Guwahati High Court upholding judgment of the Central Administrative Tribunal (for short `the Tribunal') by which direction was given to pay Stenographers of subordinate offices the same scale of pay as paid to the Stenographer Grade C in the Central Secretariat. The said direction was given by order dated 25.2.2000 in review application No. 15/98 in OA No. 151/91. Originally, by order dated 10.8.1998, the application No. 151/91 was dismissed by the Tribunal.  3. Factual background forming foundation of the subject matter of appeal is as follows :  The respondent (hereinafter referred to as `the employee') was working as a Stenographer Grade-II in the office of Geological Survey of India w.e.f. 4.1.1984. He was placed on the pay scale of Rs. 1400-40-1800-EB-50- 2300 based on the recommendations of the Central Pay Commission. There was dissatisfaction by several employees about the scales. A Board of Arbitration was constituted after agitation by some of the staff. It rejected the claim of absolute parity of pay scales of Stenographer Grade-II with that of Stenographer Grade C of the Central Secretariat. It was however recommended that the scale should be Rs. 1400-40-1600-50-2300-EB-60-2600. The Ministry of Finance (Department of Expenditure) issued OM 7(18)-E3/81 dated 4.5.1990 in this regard. On the basis of Office Memorandum dated 31.7.1990 of Department of Personnel and Training, with concurrence of Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure revised scale of pay of Stenographer Grade `C' in Central Secretariat Stenographer Service to Rs. 1640-60-2600-EB-75-2900 with effect from 1.1.1986. It is to be noted as indicated supra that on 4.5.1990 the Ministry of Finance, Department of Expenditure by its Office Memorandum dated 4.5.90 clarified that considering the demand by the National Council of JCM, matter was referred to Board of Arbitration which considered the claim on 17/18.8.1989. The claim was rejected holding that there was no parity in the pay scale of Stenographer in the subordinate offices and the Secretariat. The award was given on 18.8.1989. When the scale of pay of Rs. 1400-40-1800-EB-50-2300 was fixed pursuant to the Award by the Board of Arbitration to Rs. 1400-40-1600-50-2300-EB-60-2600, Ministry of Finance implemented the decision of the Board of Arbitration and Office Memorandum dated 4.5.90 as referred to above was issued. The Stenographers Grade-II in subordinate offices were placed in the same pay scales of Rs. 1400-2600 w.e.f. 1.1.1986. The view of Union of India was that Stenographer Grade-II are not in comparable grade with Stenographer Grade `C' in Central Secretariat. According to it, services in Stenographer Grade `C' in the Central Secretariat belong to Grade `B' whereas Stenographers Grade-II in Geological Survey of India are classified as Grade C (Ministerial). A representation was submitted by the respondent to the Deputy Director General, Geological Survey of India, Shilong, requesting to fix his pay in the revised scale of Rs. 1640-2900 in terms of Office Memorandum dated 31.7.1990. Thereafter on 10.7.1998 the respondent-employee filed O.A. No. 151/1991 before the Tribunal seeking parity of pay scale with that of Stenographer Grade `C' of the Central Secretariat. OA was dismissed by the Tribunal holding that nature of work, duties and responsibilities of the two categories of Stenographers were not the same. Subsequently on 25.2.2000 the Tribunal took a different view in the review application filed. In the review application it held that all the relevant facts were not placed before the Central Pay Commission and it has not given any reason as to why different scales were to be fixed. It was observed that nothing in the report of the Pay commission indicated that nature and duties of the employees were specifically considered. It only made the difference on the ground that workload and responsibilities of Stenographer Grade `C' of Central Secretariat are expected to be heavier. Tribunal found fault with this conclusion. It was further noted that the nature of work, duties and responsibilities of the two categories of Stenographers clearly indicate that the relevant aspects were not considered by the Commission and it proceeded on a different basis. The Tribunal was of the view that Stenographer Grade-II should be placed in the pay scale of Rs. 1640-2900 by applying the logic of equal pay for equal work. Challenge before the High Court was turned down as noted above. 4. Learned Additional Solicitor General submitted that the Tribunal's decision as well as the High Court's judgment proceeded on the concept of `equal pay for equal work'. The said dicta cannot be used in the abstract. The Tribunal as well as the High Court proceeded on erroneous premises by holding that onus to prove non-application of the concept has to be on the employer. It was pointed out that it is really not so. On the contrary the person who asserts that he is entitled to `equal pay for equal work' has to establish it. Merely because in some of the cases SLPs were dismissed that cannot be a ground to extend the benefit to the employees on the logic of `equal for equal work'.  5. In response, learned counsel for the respondent-employee submitted that earlier on the basis of a policy decision `equal pay for equal work' was being applied to both the classes of employees. Whenever there was an increase in one of the scales, it is logical that the enhanced scale should be applied across the line and uniformly. The earlier attempts of paying different scales of pay were foiled by the Tribunal and even this Court did not interfere and SLPs were dismissed. The High Court has noted that in several cases, the Tribunal and the High Court had decided similar controversies and similar pay scales were being granted. That being so, the High Court has rightly concluded that departure was not warranted. The High Court also observed that normally speaking though not necessarily all the Stenographers have almost identical duties to perform.  6. This Court in Union of India v. Pradip Kumar Dey (2000(8) SCC 580) : 2001(1) SCT 462 (SC) after referring to various decisions dealing with the similar question in para 8 has held thus : (SCC p. 584)  "8. In our considered view, the Division Bench of the High Court was not right and justified in straight away giving direction to grant pay scale to the respondent when there was no material placed before the Court for comparison to order to apply the principle of `equal pay for equal work' between the Radio Operators of CRPF and the Radio Operators working in civil side in the Central Water Commission and the Directorate of Police Wireless. In the absence of material relating to other comparable employees as to the qualifications, method of recruitment, degree of skill, experience involved in performance of job, training required, responsibilities undertaken and other facilities in addition to pay scales, the learned Single Judge was right when he stated in the order that in the absence of such material it would not possible to grant relief to the respondent. No doubt, the Directorate of CRPF made recommendations to the Pay Commission for giving higher pay scales on the basis of which claim is made by the respondent for grant of pay scale. The factual statements contained in the recommendation of a particular department alone cannot be considered per se proof of such things or they cannot by themselves vouch for the correctness of the same. The said recommendation could not be taken as a recommendation made by the Government. Even otherwise a mere recommendation did not confer any right on the respondent to make such a claim for writ of mandamus." 7. Yet, in another decision in State Bank of India v. M.R. Ganesh Babu (2002(4) SCC 556) : 2002(2) SCT 749 (SC) a Bench of three learned Judges of this Court, while dealing with the same principle, in para 16 has expressed that : (SCC p. 563)  "16. The principle of equal pay for equal work has been considered and applied in many reported decisions of this Court. The principle has been adequately explained and crystallized and sufficiently reiterated in a catena of decisions of this Court. It is well settled that equal pay must depend upon the nature of work done. It cannot be judged by the mere volume of work; there may be qualitative difference as regards reliability and responsibility. Functions may be the same but the responsibilities made a difference. One cannot deny that often the difference is a matter of degree and that there is an element of value judgment by those who are charged with the administration in fixing the scales of pay and other conditions of service. So long as such value judgment is made bona fide, reasonably on an intelligible criterion which has a rational nexus with the object of differentiation, such differentiation will not amount to discrimination. The principle is not always easy to apply as there are inherent difficulties in comparing and evaluating the work done by different persons in different organizations, or even in the same organization. Differentiation in pay scales of persons holding same posts and performing similar work on the basis of difference in the degree of responsibility, reliability and confidentiality would be a valid differentiation. The judgment of administrative authorities concerning the responsibilities which attach to the post, and the degree of reliability expected to an incumbent, would be a value judgment of the authorities concerned which, if arrived at bona fide, reasonably and rationally, was not open to interference by the court." (Also see State of Haryana and Anr. v. Tilak Raj and Ors. (2003(6) SCC 123) and Orissa University of Agriculture & Technology and Anr. v. Manoj K. Mohannty (2003(5) SCC 188) : 2003(2) SCT 971 (SC)). 8. In this case, the Tribunal and High Court seem to have completely lost sight of the fact that the Fifth Pay Commission specifically considered the question and held that there is no question of any equivalence. The Commission observed as follows :  "46.34. We have given our careful consideration to the suggestions made by Associations representing Stenographers in Offices outside the Secretariat in the light of observations made by the Third CPC. The Commission had observed that as a general statement, it was correct to say that the basis nature of a Stenographer's work remained by and large the same whether he was working with an officer in the Secretariat or with an officer in a subordinate office. The Commission was of the considered view, that the size of the Stenographer's job was very much dependent upon the nature of work entrusted to that officer and that it would not be correct, therefore, to go merely by the status in disregard of the functional requirement. By the very nature of work in the secretariat, the volume of dictation and typing work was expected to be heavier than in a subordinate office, the requirement of secrecy even in civil offices of the secretariat could be very stringent. Considering the differences is the hierarchical structures and in the type of work transacted the Commission was not in favour of adopting a uniform pattern in respect of matter listed in the preceding paragraph. To our mind, the observations of the Third CPC are as relevant today as they were at that point of time and we are not inclined to overlook them totally. In view of the abovementioned distinguishable feature, we do not concede the demand for absolute parity in regard to pay scales between stenographers in officers outside the secretariat and in the secretariat notwithstanding the fact that some petitioner Stenographers Grade II have got other benefit of parity in pay scale through courts. However, pursuing the policy enunciated by the Second CPC that disparity in the pay scale prescribed for stenographers in the Secretariat and the non-secretariat organisations should be reduced as far as possible, we are of the view that Stenographers Grade II should be placed in the existing pay scale of Rs. 1600-2660 instead of Rs. 1400-2300/Rs. 1400- 2600." 9. Strangely, the Tribunal in the review petition came to hold that the Commission had not based its conclusion on any data. It is trite law that it is not open for any Court to sit in judgment as on appeal over the conclusion of the Commission. Further the Tribunal and the High Court proceeded as if it was the employer who was to show that there was no equality in the work. On the contrary the person who asserts that there is equality has to prove it. The equality is not based on designation or the nature of work alone. There are several other factors like, responsibilities, reliabilities, experience, confidentially involved, functional need and requirements commensurate with the position in the hierarchy, the qualifications required which are equally relevant.  10. In State of W.B. and Ors. v. Hari Narayan Bhowal and Ors. (1994(4) SCC 78) : 1994(3) SCT 707 (SC), it was observed :  "This Court in the case of Delhi Veterinary Ass. v. Union of India (1984(3) SCC 1) said that in addition to the principle of `equal pay for equal work', the pay structure of the employees of the Government should reflect many other social values. It was said : "The degree of skill, strain of work, experience involved, training required, responsibility undertaken, mental and physical requirements, disagreeableness of the task, hazard attendant on work and fatigue involved are, according to the Third Pay Commission, some of the relevant factors which should be taken into consideration in fixing pay scales. The method of recruitment, the level of which the initial recruitment is made in the hierarchy of service or cadre, minimum educational and technical qualifications prescribed for the post, the nature of dealings with the public, avenues of promotion available and horizontal and vertical relativity with other jobs in the same service or outside are also relevant factors." 11. In the case of State of U.P. v. J.P. Chaurasia (1989(1) SCC 121) it was pointed out that whether two posts are equal or should carry the equal pay, depends on several factors. It does not depend just upon either the nature of work or the volume of work done. Primarily it requires among others, evaluation of duties and responsibilities of the respective posts by the Competent Authorities constituted for the purpose and Courts cannot ordinately substitute themselves in the place of those authorities. The quantity of work may be the same but the quality may be different. That cannot be determined by relying upon averments in affidavits of interested parties. It must be determined by expert bodies like Pay Commission and the Government, who would be the best judges, to evaluate the nature of duty, responsibility and all relevant factors. The same view reiterated in the case of State of M.P. v. Pramod Bhartiya (1993(1) SCC 539) : 1993(1) SCT 138 (SC) by a three-Judge Bench of this Court. In the case of Shyam Babu Verma v. Union of India (1994(2) SCC 521) : 1994(2) SCT 296 (SC) a claim for equal pay by a group of Pharmacists was rejected saying that the classification made by a body of experts after full study and analysis of the work, should not be disturbed except for strong reasons which indicate that the classification made was unreasonable.  12. These aspects have been completely lost sight of by the Tribunal and the High Court.  13. The Tribunal passed the impugned order by reviewing the earlier order. A bare reading of the two orders shows that the order in review application was in complete variation and disregard of the earlier order and the strong as well as sound reasons contained therein whereby the original application was rejected. The scope for review is rather limited and it is not permissible for the forum hearing the review application to act as an appellate authority in respect of the original order by a fresh and rehearing of the matter to facilitate a change of opinion on merits. The Tribunal seems to have transferred its jurisdiction in dealing with the review petition as if it was hearing original application. This aspect has also not been noticed by the High Court.  14. Looked at from any angle, the judgment fo the Tribunal in review application and of the High Court confirming it have no leg to stand. They deserve to be set aside which we direct. The appeal is allowed.  Costs made easy.  Appeal allowed.
summary:
A. Constitution of India, Articles 14 and 16 - Equal Pay for equal work - Determining whether two posts should carry the same pay depends not only on whether the work is equal, but also on other factors such as the nature and volume of work and responsibilities attached to the post - Stenography at higher level posts cannot be compared to that at lower level posts. [Paras 9 and 11]
B. Review - Limited Scope of Review - The Court's authority in review is restricted, as it cannot re-examine the case and completely ignore the original order under review, as this would exceed its jurisdiction. [Para 13]

text: Syed Bashir-ud-Din, J. - Petitioner, an Executive Engineer of Rural Engineering Wing of the Rural Development Department of the Government on transfer from Kargil was transferred vide Respondent No. 7 as Executive Engineer, REW, Anantnag vice Government Order No : 261-GR(RD) of 2002 dated 24.10.2002. However, this order was withdrawn by the Principal Secretary to Government, Rural Development Department vide Government Order No : 278/RD of 2002 dated 18.11.2002. This order (Annexure-F) is impugned in the writ petition on grounds alleged in the petition. Alongwith the writ petition CMP No : 2537/2002 was moved for seeking stay of the impugned order and thereby allowing petitioner to work as Ex-Engineer, REW, Anantang. At motion stage, the court issued the following order on 22.11.2002, in the main as also in the interim matter :-  "Mr. A.M. Dar, Advocate for petitioner. Issue Notice to the respondents for filing objections. Issue notice in the CMP also. In the meanwhile, the operation of the impugned order No : 278-RD of 2002 dated 18.11.2002 is stayed, till next date before the bench. The order shall however be subject to objections of the other side and shall be subject to amendment/alteration on motion. Learned counsel for the petitioner to take steps for effective service." However, the respondent No. 7 who was on Caveat, moved an application for vacation/modification of the above court other. The counsel for the respondent No. 7 complains that despite having moved Caveat, he was neither served with the notice in the matter nor at all heard and yet the impugned order was passed. It appears that the Caveat was not brought to the notice of the court when the impugned order was passed. But all the same having noticed the Caveat and the motion/objections on record for amendment/alteration of the initial interim direction, the parties were heard on the entire gambit of the interim relief prayed for.  2. Petitioner, a resident of Kargil served as Executive Engineer, REW at Kargil for long 13 years. He developed a serious health problem and sought transfer to the Valley & even filed a writ petition 962/99, which was disposed of on 3.11.1999 with direction to respondents to consider the case and take a decision thereto. He was examined by the Medical Board of the Government of Jammu and Kashmir and it was noted that the person of Shri M.D. Khan, "has clinical presentation suggestive of prinzmetal's variant angina. He is advised to report to the department of Cardiology Medical College hospital Srinagar/SKIMS Sora Srinagar...." and was further advised among other things to avoid stay at high altitude. The Government, "on medical and humanitarian grounds", transferred and posted him as Executive Engineer, Anantnag vice Mr. Nazir Ahmad Sofi, Respondent No. 7, who was directed to sop (swap ?) posting with the petitioner as Executive Engineer, REW Kargil (Order dated 24.10.2002, (Annexure-C). Annexures D and E ex facie indicate that the petitioner assumed charge at Anantnag from 26.6.2002 (though not as per prescribed format) and at the same time complained to Director Rural Development Department Srinagar, that his predecessor in office at Anantnag (Respondent No. 7) used un- parliamentary language against him and threatened him to use anti social elements against him (Annexure-H). The Government subsequently on 18.11.2002 has withdrawn the order and attached the petitioner with Director Rural Development Department Kashmir Srinagar.  3. Ld. counsel for the petitioner refers Annexure-G, which appears to be an interim direction of the Ld. Single Bench, requiring the parties to maintain status quo in writ petition No. 1345/2002 and CMP No : 2399/2002. However, neither the nature not the subject of this writ petition or the CMP, is indicated. It is not also shown if this direction was within the knowledge of respondents. In any case, the direction simply says that the parties shall maintain status quo for one week. Whether this order was communicated to other side and by whom it was to be observed, is not clear.  4. Respondent No. 7, the successor in office of petitioner at Anantnag has submitted that the order was withdrawn/modified on his presentation, because he had just eight months to retire and having regard to his age it would cause great hardship to him if he was to work at Kargil.........more so at the fag end end of his service when he is completing his papers for retiral benefits. His representation to the Government was accepted and order was withdrawn.  5. The counsel for respondents Mr. M.H. Attar has also made submission in line with the objections and further states that the petitioner's order of posting to Anantnag which has been subsequently withdrawn is not an order which is either in the interest of public or in the interest of administration. Instead the order itself says that it has been passed "on medical and humanitarian grounds" as the petitioner has worked at Kargil for more than 13 years. By withdrawal of this order, no public or administrative interest has suffered and therefore, petitioner has no right to challenge the order of withdrawal (Annexure-F) of such order passed on grounds personal to petitioner. (Annexure-C).  6. The Government and its officials including those of Rural Dev. Department have not appeared to contest, possibly as the arrangements are reported not in place for attending the cases filed on behalf of or against the Government and its officials. Be that as it may, the interim direction in the matter cannot await such arrangement to come about, of which arrangement signs to come by are far off.  7. On consideration, having regard to the totality of facts and circumstances of this case, it is a fact that petitioner's order of transfer and posting to Anantnag is purely on medical and humanitarian grounds and not the least in the interest of administration or public interest. Withdrawal of such an order by subsequent impugned government order is not equally shown in the interest of administration or public interest. The order simply says that it has been passed to comply with the desire of Minister of Rural Dev. Department. Equally is the consideration that respondent No. 7 is retiring within eight months and cannot at such age at the peak of winter be asked to serve at Kargil when even the rules/circulars on the subject of transfer to Kargil and Leh, do not permit such a course.  8. Looking at the problem from any angle, it appears that the petitioner and the respondent No. 7 are fighting it out in between themselves, who among the two is to hold the post of Executive Engineer, REW Anantnag and for the purpose have not placed the matter in true colour and spirit before the competent authority/government. On one hand a person with serious cardio health problem is desperate to retain the posting at Anantnag and on the other hand the person with just 8 months to go on superannuation, is trying his every bit to cling and hang on to the post at Anantnag. Keeping either at the place would serve neither any public interest nor any interest of administration. It appears that the post of Executive Engineer, REW Anantnag is reduced to personal property by the two officers, engaged in mud slugging duel to show each other down. In the process, interest of public are to suffer and the measures need to be taken to remedy the situation. The Government would do well immediately to consider the matter and pass orders appointing some suitable hand and giving charge of the post of Executive Engineer REW Anantnag to a third person (Ex. Engineer, REW), while keeping out these two rival contenders to the post of REW Executive Engineer, Anantnag. Neither is fit enough to hold the post. This direction just and proper as it is, is passed in the tell tale facts and circumstances of the case to serve greater public interests. The Government shall comply with this direction within two weeks. Copy of the order besides being sent in the normal course, shall be faxed to Principal Secretary to Government Rural Development Department at Jammu for compliance. The compliance shall be reported to the court.  Order accordingly.
summary: The Constitution of India's Articles 14 and 226 state that transfer should be in the public interest, and in cases where rival claims are made for a post, two officers who prioritize their own interests over public welfare by ignoring personal health problems and age factors are deemed unsuitable for the position. This highlights the importance of appointing a third suitable candidate to the crucial post. [Paras 7 and 8]

text: G.B. Pattanaik, J. - These appeals are directed against the impugned order of the Karnataka State Administrative Tribunal. The appellant on the death of his father was given a compassionate appointment as Second Division Assistant/Clerks, even though he had applied for the post of Sub-Inspector of Excise and did possess the necessary qualification for the said post. Respondents 3 and 4 whose father also died while in service were appointed similarly as Second Division Assistant/Clerk on 9.1.1978 and 19.12.1979 respectively. Those respondents 3 and 4 while continuing as Second Division Assistant/Clerk were later on promoted/appointed as Sub-Inspector of Excise on 3.10.1987 and 27.4.1988. The appellant who had been earlier appointed on compassionate ground as Second Division Assistant/Clerk and was entitled to be considered for appointment as Sub-Inspector of Excise was not considered when the respondents 3 and 4 were appointed as Sub-Inspector of Excise. The appellant therefore moved the State Administrative Tribunal claiming that his case for appointment as Sub-Inspector of Excise be considered or in the alternative the appointment of respondents 3 and 4 be quashed. The Tribunal considered the application of the appellant and did not grant the relief of his case being considered for appointment as Sub-Inspector of Excise. The Tribunal, however, quashed the appointment of respondents 3 and 4 as Sub- Inspector of Excise. Against the aforesaid order, the State of Karnataka had approached this Court in Special Leave Petition but that Special Leave Petition stood dismissed. The respondents 3 and 4 however, approached this Court against the order quashing their appointment as Sub-Inspector of Excise. This Court, however made some observations in that Special Leave Petition and permitted the respondents 3 and 4 to file an application for review before the State Administrative Tribunal. Pursuance to the aforesaid order of this Court, the respondents 3 and 4 having approached the Tribunal for review of the earlier order, the Tribunal by the impugned order reviewed its earlier order and did not interfere with the appointment of respondents 3 and 4 on the ground that the appellant has moved the Tribunal against the appointment of respondents 3 and 4 belatedly and therefore the same could not be interfered with. It is this review order of the Tribunal which is the subject-matter of the challenge in the present appeals.  2. The learned counsel for the appellant contended that even though the respondents 3 and 4's appointment could not be assailed on the ground of belated approach by the appellant but the prayer' with regard to consideration of the appellant for the post of Sub-Inspector of Excise could not have been rejected by the Tribunal. The learned counsel appearing for the State Government on the other hand, contended that against the earlier order when the Tribunal denied the relief of considering the case of the appellant for the post of Sub-Inspector of Excise, the appellant having not moved this Court, the same has become final and therefore should not be interfered with by this Court. There is some force in the aforesaid contention of the learned counsel for the State. But having considered the facts and circumstances of the present case and admittedly the respondents 3 and 4, who were similarly situated like the appellant and who were given compassionate appointment later than the appellant, having been appointed as Sub-Inspector of Excise, the appellant has a justifiable grievance. It is true that the appointment on compassionate ground in the State of Karnataka is not governed by any statutory rules but by set of administrative instruction and as such is not enforceable in a Court of Law. But the grounds on which the appellant makes out the case for consideration of his case, is the violation of Article 14 and discriminatory treatment meted out to the appellant. It is undisputed that the date on which the appellant was given a compassionate appointment as the Second Division Assistant/Clerk he had the necessary qualification for being appointed as Sub-Inspector of Excise. It is also undisputed that the respondents 3 and 4 were given appointment initially as Second Division Assistant/Clerk but later than the appellant. When the State therefore thought it fit to change the post of respondents 3 and 4 and appointed them to the post of Sub-Inspector of Excise, unless there is any justifiable reason exist, there is no reason as to why the appellant should be treated with a hostile discrimination. In the aforesaid circumstances, we set aside the impugned order of the Tribunal rejecting the prayer of the appellant for being considered for the post of Sub-Inspector of Excise and we direct that the State Government may consider the case of appointment of the appellant as Sub-Inspector of Excise. Be it stated, in the event he is appointed it would be prospective and he will not be entitled to any retrospective benefit. The appeals are allowed accordingly.  Appeals allowed.
summary: Constitution of India, Article 16 - Compassionate appointment - Discrimination - Appellant and respondents were appointed as clerks under compassionate appointment, despite being eligible for the post of Sub-Inspector of Excise. Later, the respondents were promoted to Sub-Inspectors, while the senior appellant was overlooked. The Tribunal initially quashed the appointment of respondents but refused relief to appellant, citing delay in filing the case. The review Tribunal did not interfere with respondents' appointment and did not grant relief to the appellant. The order was challenged, and it was held that the appellant must be considered for the post of Sub-Inspector, and discrimination against the appellant cannot be justified. The order of the Tribunal was set aside, and the State was directed to consider the appellant's case for the appointment of a Sub-Inspector of Excise. The appeal was allowed accordingly. [Paras 1 and 2]

text: M.M. Kumar, J. - By this order two writ petitions, namely, C.W.P. No. 15371 of 2000 and C.W.P. No. 4579 of 2002 are proposed to be disposed of because the relief claimed by the petitioner relates to his service career involving different stages. The petitioner approached this Court by filing first petition with a prayer for releasing him revised pay scale of Rs. 12000-420- 18300 with a pay fixation of Rs. 14940/- w.e.f. 1.1.1996 at par with other Assistant Professors of Regional Engineering College, Kurukshetra (respondent No. 4). He also claimed arrears on account of pay revision which were wrongly denied to him alongwith interest @ 18 percent p.a. from 1.12.1999 asserting that similarly situated Assistant Professors in the Regional Engineering College (respondent No. 4) were paid the same pay scale. Further direction was sought to respondents to confirm the petitioner as Assistant Professor by placing reliance on Bye-law 11 of the Bye-laws framed by the Regional Engineering College (Kurukshetra) Society as the petitioner had already completed three years period probation and accordingly to include his name at the appropriate place in the inter-departmental seniority list of the College.  2. The second petition came to be filed on 28.2.2002 when one month's notice was issued to the petitioner for dispensing with his services in the Enterpreneurship Development Cell (for brevity the ED Cell) w.e.f. 31.3.2002. A prayer has been made for quashing the afore-mentioned notice with all consequential benefits. A further prayer has been made for quashing the decision taken by the Board of Governors on agenda item No. 94.26 in its meeting held on 19.11.2001. According to the afore-mentioned decision, the Board of Governors had dis-agreed to merge the ED Cell with the College and had authorised the Principal to terminate services of the petitioner. The petitioner has also prayed for a direction to the respondents to merge ED Cell with the College in terms of the guide-lines issued by the Ministry of Science and Technology (National Enterpreneurship Development Board Division), New Delhi, respondent No. 1.  3. Brief facts of the case are required to be examined by referring to the background which led to establishment of ED Cell at the Regional Engineering College, Kurukshetra (respondent No. 4) :  Enterpreneurship Development Cell  4. There is an Enterpreneurship Development Board working under the Ministry of Science and Technology of the Union of India (for brevity, "the NSTEDB"). A Scheme was framed by NSTEDB for establishing ED Cell in various technical institutions including Regional Engineering College, Kurukshetra. It is appropriate to mention that the object of establishing ED Cell is to utilise the potential expertise and enthusiasm which has been shown in the field of enterpreneurship development by the technical institutions so that adequate infrastructure facilities may be created which may require to promote the activities of the NSTEDB on regional basis. In order to establish ED Cell a Advisory Committee was constituted under the NSTEDB and guide-lines were framed for establishing the ED Cell. A photo-copy of the guide-lines have been placed on record as Annexure P.8. A glance at the guide-lines (Annexure P.8) would show at the first instance that the Department of Science and Technology was to provide financial support to ED Cell on yearly basis and thereafter the responsibility was to shift on the educational institutions/Regional Engineering Colleges to arrange funds for running the ED Cell and to absorb the faculty and staff in the normal stream of the College/University after the period of assistance has expired. There is a requirement specified in the guide-lines that a certificate/affidavit in the form of Appendix "A" was required to be furnished to that effect. According to Clause 5 of the Certificate it is required to be undertaken by the educational institution/Regional Engineering College where ED Cell is established that it would be their responsibility to absorb ED Cell established alongwith its staff and arrange funds for the same after the expiry of period of assistance from the Department of Science and Technology, Union of India. One such ED Cell was established at the Regional Engineering College, Kurukshetra.  Brief Facts :  5. On 1.4.1989, respondent No. 4 issued an advertisement in the English Daily, Hindustan Times (Annexure P.1) for appointment to the post of Chief Project Coordinator in the pre-revised scale of Rs. 1500-2500 (revised to Rs. 4500- 7300). The petitioner has a meritorious academic record. He has done Master of Engineering (System Engineering and Operations Research) from the University of Roorkee with Gold Medal by securing 88 percent marks in the year 1978 after he acquired the degree of B.Sc. Engineering (Electrical) from the Punjab Engineering College, Chandigarh in 1975 by securing 67.7 percent marks in the first division. It is claimed by the petitioner that he possessed professional training and experience in his field by undergoing courses with reputed companies like Suzuki Motor Company Ltd., Japan and Steel Authority of India Ltd. Durgapur Steel Plant, TATA Burroughs Ltd. etc. etc. The petitioner fulfilled all the essential qualifications mentioned in the advertisement (Annexure P.1) and applied. Alongwith the application the petitioner sent all the necessary certificates showing his qualifications and his detailed bio- data explaining his experience and other abilities. He was interviewed in pursuance of the letter dated 8.6.1969 and was selected for appointment to the post of Senior Project Leader as is evident from the letter of appointment dated 9.8.1989 (Annexure P.2). The appointment letter provided that he would be allowed basic pay of Rs. 1600/- in the unrevised pay scale of Rs. 1200-1900 and his total emoluments would be Rs. 4630/- excluding HRA. It was further indicated that it would be equivalent to the stage of Rs. 3700/- in the revised scale of Rs. 3700-5700. The revision was to follow shortly as it was awaiting the approval of the State Government, respondent No. 3. The petitioner was asked to join his duties by 16.2.1990 which he accordingly joined. The nomenclature of the ED Cell was changed into Centre for Industrial Liaison and Technical Developments (for brevity "the Centre") by the Board of Governors of respondent No. 4 in its meeting held on 23.2.1991. It was resolved to approve the staff structure of the Centre and the pay scales. The name of the post of Senior Project Leader, to which the petitioner was appointed on 9.8.1989 was re-designated as Assistant Professor in the Centre in the pay scale of Rs. 3700-5700. A copy of the minutes of the meeting has been placed on record as Annexure P.3. His pay scale was also revised by respondent No. 4 in the scale of Rs. 3700-5700. On 5.11.1999 (Annexure P.4) a notification was issued with regard to the revision of pay scales of teachers in the various Colleges and other Degree level Technical Institutions in the State of Haryana and pay scale of Assistant Professor was revised from Rs. 3700-5700 to Rs. 12000-420-18300. On the completion of five years of service in the grade the pay was required to be fixed at Rs. 14,940/-. However, the petitioner was not granted the afore-mentioned revised scale despite the fact that other similarly situated Assistant Professors working in respondent No. 4 College had been granted the pay scale of Rs. 12000-18300 w.e.f. 1.12.1999. The petitioner submitted a representation in this regard dated 1.12.1999 (Annexure P.5) to the Principal of respondent No. 4 requesting him that necessary steps may be taken to pay him the salary and the allowances in the revised scale of pay of Rs. 14940-18300 (as he has already completed five years of service in that grade). The inaction on the part of respondents No. 3 and 4 resulted into issuance of reminder and a representation to respondent No. 3 on 30.5.2000 (Annexure P.6). In order to verify whether the benefit of revised pay scales have been extended to the teachers working in the ED Cell of other Colleges, respondent No. 4 wrote a letter to the Calicut Regional Engineering College. In response thereto the Calicut Regional Engineering College has replied on 24.5.2000 affirming that revised pay scales have been given to the staff working in the ED Cell. It is also pertinent to mention that respondent No. 4 was required to merge the ED Cell into the normal stream of the institution and the expenses were to be met from their sources or from the income generated by the ED Cell after the period of three years of financial assistance received from the Department of Science and Technology. At this stage, the petitioner filed the first writ petition claiming the benefit of revised pay scale alongwith the prayer for some other relief.  6. After the receipt of notice of the first writ petition, it is alleged that respondent No. 5 namely Shri N.P. Mehta, Principal, Regional Engineering College, Kurukshetra developed a prejudice against the petitioner because he started taking steps to wind up ED Cell in order to succeed in dispensing with the services of the petitioner. Certain other allegations have also been levelled against respondent No. 5. Various steps as listed in the writ petition reads as under :  i) Firstly, the petitioner was in line to be allotted House No. BB4 in the campus of the college. On 24th March, 2001 that house was allotted to another Assistant Professor 7 years junior to the petitioner. ii) An order was made by respondent No. 5 on 1.6.2001 completely stopping the salary of the petitioner. The petitioner submitted representation on 1.6.2001 and a reminder on 5.6.2001 requesting respondent No. 5 to release his salary. In response to the said letter, however, respondent No. 5 asked the petitioner to arrange the non-plan funds for his salary himself and the salary for the month of May 2001 was released on 21.6.2001 as "a goodwill gesture". A copy of the representation dated 1.6.2001 and reply dated 18.6.2001 is annexed as Annexure P.9 and P.10 respectively. iii) That apart from the above, other letters were written for the return of equipment etc. worth Rs. 1.898 lakhs of the ED Cell and regarding occupation of rooms of the building of the ED Cell. The building was constructed out of the funds provided by the Government of India for the ED Cell. These rooms were/are meant fo the ED Cell only. The letters were written to make the ED Cell viable for its own self. The amounts as claimed are of the ED Cell and if the same are credited to its accounts, the Cell would have its own resources. iv) That thereafter the petitioner was not paid salary for the month of July, 2001. On account of non-receipt of salary and other biased attitude of the Principal of respondent No. 4 College, he suffered heart attack and was admitted in the local Hospital on 15.8.2001. He was referred to PGI, Chandigarh on 16.8.2001 and he was admitted in PGI on 18.8.2001. The petitioner underwent Open Heart Bye Pass Surgery on 28.9.2001. v) That the petitioner, thereafter, rejoined his duty after 50 days leave on 9.10.2001 and it was found that he has not been paid salary for the months of August and September, 2001. The petitioner submitted his medical bills also for a sum of Rs. 74,492.71 to respondent No. 4 on 31.10.2001. What to talk of the reimbursement of medical bills, the petitioner was not paid salary for the months of October, 2001 even. The petitioner then sent SOS representation to respondent No. 4 on 7.11.2001. Thereafter, a week before the meeting of the Board of Governors, the petitioner received five months salary i.e. from July to October, 2001 on 13.11.2001. However, now again from January 2002 onwards no salary has been released to the petitioner." 7. It has further been averred that respondent No. 5 presented an agenda (Annexure P.11) before the Board of Governors to consider the absorption of faculty of the ED Cell with the main stream of respondent No. 4 i.e. Regional Engineering College. The agenda is alleged to be factually incorrect. It has also been pointed out by the petitioner that the Committee on 25.9.2000 had already recommended (Annexure P.12) that ED Cell should be merged with respondent No. 4 in accordance with the mandatory directions of respondent Nos. 1 and 2 as per the specific undertaking furnished by respondent No. 4. Even respondent No. 1 in a communication dated 17.9.1999 (Annexure P.3) has insisted for continuation of ED Cell after 31.3.2002 when the financial assistance was stopped. It is alleged that in the agenda (Annexure P.11) presented to the Board of Governors factually incorrect information was given by stating that except for the petitioner two posts of Junior Stenographer and Peon were never filled up. It is alleged that one Shri Prem Kumar was appointed as Steno-typist in the ED Cell on a consolidated salary vide order dated 15.9.1989 and he had been absorbed in the main stream of the College vide order dated 1.2.1991. Thereafter one Shashi Bala was appointed as Steno- typist in the ED Cell on 7.8.1995 who has been absorbed on 7.8.1995 vide Annexure P.16. Another case cited is that of Davender Singh who was alleged to have been appointed as Stenographer in the Cell on 11.4.1997 and thereafter he was transferred to the main stream by posting him in the office of the Principal vide Annexures P.17 to P.19.  8. The petitioner has also pointed out vide his representation dated 12.2.2002 that number of posts were vacant and the petitioner could have been sent to the Electrical Engineering department as Assistant Professor because he had been given teaching load of the regular academic course to teach students of respondent No. 4 College. A certificate issued by the Chairman Electrical Engineering Department of respondent No. 4 College dated 20.9.2000 shows that petitioner has been given teaching load of 12 periods per week which is equivalent to the teaching periods of an Assistant Professor. The same was withdrawn lateron at the instance of respondent No. 4 for which a representation (Annexure P.23) was filed by the petitioner.  9. The Board of Governors in its meeting held on 19.11.2001 refused to merge the ED Cell with the College advising that efforts should be made to secure some more Scheme or Project sponsored by the College where the petitioner might be adjusted. As a consequence one month's notice was served on the petitioner on 28.2.2002 stating therein that the financial assistance to the ED Cell was available only upto 31.3.2002 and his services are liable to be dispensed with w.e.f 31.3.2002 (Annexure P.24).  10. In the written statement filed on behalf of respondents No. 1 and 2 the stand taken is that after the assistance by the Department of Science and Technology and NSTEDB had come to end it was the responsibility of respondent No. 4 to continue the ED Cell and arrange funds for the same. It has been further averred in para 12 of the written statement that ED Cell should merge into the normal stream of the institute for running on a continuing basis. The expenses were to met from the sources of the institute or from the income generated by the ED Cell through consultancy etc. Similar stand has been taken in paras 16 and 17 of the reply.  11. In the written statement filed by respondents No. 4 and 5 the stand taken with regard to creation of posts and change of nomenclature of the post by the Board of Governors in its 77th meeting is that the posts which were created could not be materialised on account of paucity of funds and the petitioner was never offered the post of Assistant Professor. It is asserted that the petitioner continues to hold the post of Senior Project Leader in the pay scale of Rs. 3700-5700. It is further stated that the Department of Science and Technology sent a letter dated 17.9.1999 (Annexure R/4/1) that respondent No. 4 was to ensure continuation of ED Cell after the financial assistance by the Department of Science and Technology was to come to end on 31.3.2002. A Committee was constituted to look into the details with regard to the continuation of ED Cell and its merger with respondent No. 4. The Committee submitted its report dated 25.9.2000 (Annexure R.4.2) favourably recommending merger in view of the mandatory directions issued by the Department of Science and Technology and the undertaking given by the College. However, it has been asserted that the Board of Governors in its meeting held on 19.11.2001 vide agenda item No. 94.26 did not agree to merge the ED Cell with respondent No. 4 and advised to make efforts to get some Scheme/Projects sponsored from All India Council of Technical Education where the petitioner could be associated with that Scheme-Project/Cell. Copies of agenda item and its minutes are appended as Annexures R/4/3 and R/4/4 respectively.  12. On the question of revision of pay scales, the stand taken is that the petitioner was never appointed as Assistant Professor by respondent No. 4 and there was no question of grant of any revised pay scale being given to the incumbents to the posts of Assistant Professors. It is further asserted that respondent No. 4 sent the case of the petitioner for grant of revised pay scale to the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India, which declined the request of the petitioner on the ground that ED Cell was being promoted by the Department in a project mode and no revision is to be given. A copy of the communication has been placed on the record as Annexure R/4/5.  13. It is appropriate to point out that the Department of Science and Technology had advised respondent No. 4 to consider the payment of arrears to the petitioner from its own funds as the petitioner was never merged with the faculty of the college. The example of Calicut Engineering College has also been ignored where the staff of ED Cell was merged into College. It is pertinent to mention that evasive reply has been filed with regard to the filing of affidavit by respondent No. 4 in the form of Appendix "A" to the guide-lines (Annexure P.8) wherein the undertaking is required to be given that after the financial assistance from the Department of Science and Technology is stopped, then the institution/College was to absorb the ED Cell with its faculty staff in the usual academic stream of the institution/College. In other words, the afore-mentioned stand of the petitioner has to be accepted as correct. It is claimed by respondents No. 4 and 5 that even if it is assumed that certificate in the form of Appendix "A" was filed the merger of ED Cell was not automatic and the Board of Governors was still to take a decision to which the Board of Governors never agreed.  14. That with regard to absorption of other staff it has been stated that Prem Kumar was initially selected as Steno-typist in the ED Cell and he joined as such on 18.9.1989. Lateron the College issued advertisement to fill up two posts of Steno typists on regular basis against which Prem Kumar also applied and called for interview/test. Junior Staff Selection Committee on 5.1.1991 recommended his case and he was offered appointment as Steno-typist vide appointment letter dated 1.2.1991. With regard to Shashi Bala it has been asserted that she was already holding a substantive post of Clerk in the College and was merely posted in the ED Cell. Subsequently, she was sent back to her substantive post on which she was lateron selected on regular post. Similar stand has been taken with regard to Davender Singh who was initially appointed as Senior Stenographer in the ED Cell and lateron he was selected by the Junior Staff Selection Committee on 24.12.1998. It is claimed that there is no provision for accommodating the petitioner on a vacant post. The teaching duties performed by the petitioner were assigned to him in response to his request as well as to keep him apprised that teaching is part of his duties in the ED Cell. However, it has not been denied that there are number of vacant posts for which the petitioner is duly qualified and his services could be accommodated as Assistant Professor like the Department of Electrical Engineering.  15. On 10.9.2003, a doubt has arisen about the maintainability of the writ petition as reliance was placed on the bye-laws framed by respondent No. 4. It was directed that copy of the Rules known as Regional Engineering College (Kurukshetra) Society Rules be placed on record with a copy to the counsel for the petitioner. Accordingly, a copy of the Memorandum of Association and the Rules relating to the establishment of respondent No. 4 has been placed on record. The question about the amenability of the respondent No. 4 to the writ jurisdiction of this Court shall be considered at the appropriate stage.  Submissions of petitioner :  16. Shri P.S. Patwalia, learned counsel for the petitioner has argued that respondent No. 4 is under a legal obligation to merge the ED Cell with the College. To substantiate his argument, the learned counsel has placed reliance on the advertisement Annexure P.1 to show that although the post of Chief Project Coordinator was temporary but it was likely to continue. He has also placed reliance on the recommendations of the Advisory Committee of the College comprising of Dr. S.K. Sharma, Chairman, Professor in charge ED Cell, REC Kurukshetra, Dr. S.K. Chakarvarti, Member, Professor in charge, Academic Affairs, REC Kurukshetra and R.K. Arora, Member, Deputy Registrar (Accounts) REC Kurukshetra. Reliance has also been placed by the learned counsel on agenda item No. 77.30 where the Board of Governors has considered the establishment of Centre at the College and the nomenclature of the post of Senior Project Leader/Coordinator was changed to Assistant professor. Learned counsel has also made a pointed reference to agenda item No. 94.26 by arguing that entirely incorrect facts were placed before the Board of Governors because it was stated that two posts of Junior Stenographers and Peon were never filled up in the ED Cell which have now been admitted in the written statement to be filled up. Learned counsel has maintained that on 17.9.1999 the Department of Science and Technology has infact directed respondent No. 4 to ensure continuation of ED Cell beyond 31.3.2002 when the financial assistance to respondent No. 4 was to be finally stopped.  17. Another argument raised by the learned counsel is that a discriminatory attitude has been adopted by respondent No. 5 by absorbing members of the staff like Stenographers and Peons except the petitioner. He has referred to the averments made in para 18 of the written statement filed by respondent Nos. 4 and 5 admitted that Prem Kumar and Davender Kumar were appointed as Steno typist and Senior Stenographer respectively in the ED Cell on a consolidated salary. However, before the Board of Governors, respondent No. 5 placed incorrect facts by stating that the post of Stenographer and Peon were never filled up. Learned counsel then argued that while considering agenda item No. 74.27 for establishing Centre at the respondent No. 4 College it was resolved to integrate the activities of ED Cell and the decision was taken to absorb the staff of ED Cell.  18. Learned counsel in the end has referred to mala-fide intention of respondent No. 5 on account of the fact that petitioner has filed a writ petition claiming revised pay scale. Mr. Patwalia has referred to the action of respondent No. 5 in the allotment of the house, stopping the salary of the petitioner and return of equipment worth Rs. 1,89,000/- belonging to ED Cell and regarding occupation of rooms of the building of the ED Cell. He has also referred to non-payment of salary for the month of July, 2001 and the biased attitude of the Principal which caused such a stress to the petitioner that he suffered a heart attack and was eventually admitted to P.G.I. and underwent open heart bye-pass surgery on 28.9.2001. His medical bills were not paid nor the salary for the month of October, 2001 onwards was paid. However, he received the salary before the meeting of the Board of Governors for a period of five months from July, 2001 to October, 2001 which was paid on 13.11.2001 and again from January 2002 onwards no salary has been paid. In support of his submission, the learned counsel has placed reliance on the judgement of the Supreme Court in the case of Ajay Hasia v. Khalid Mujib, AIR 1981 SC 487 and argued that the Regional Engineering Colleges are the instrumentality of the State within the meaning of Article 12 of the Constitution and therefore there is an obligation on them to act fairly. He has also placed reliance on two judgments in the cases of Pant Raj Sachdev v. The Indian Red Cross Society and ors., 1988(1) RSJ 719 and J.N. Gahlaut and ors. v. Indian Red Cross Society, Haryana and others, 2002(2) RSJ 719 : 2002(3) SCT 328 (P&H). Learned counsel has been placed reliance on another judgment of the Supreme Court in the case of G. Govinda Rajulu v. The Andhra Pradesh State Construction Corporation Ltd. and another, AIR 1987 SC 1801 and Haryana Tanneries Employees Union v. State of Haryana and another, 2002(2) RSJ 619.  Submissions of Respondent No. 4 :  19. Shri A.S. Virk, learned counsel for respondent No. 4 has argued that the petitioner has never been an employee of the Regional Engineering College and in the absence of any absorption he cannot be imposed upon on the College. He has made a reference to Annexure P.11 wherein the decision has been taken by the Board of Governors refusing to merge the ED Cell with the College. Learned counsel has drawn my pointed attention to the suggestion made by Dr. P.N. Rajdan, a representative of All India Council of Technical Education to make various efforts to get some scheme/project sponsored for the College from AIEECT and associate the petitioner with such scheme/project. Referring to Annexure P.3 wherein establishment of Centre was approved, the learned counsel has argued that on account of paucity of funds the same could not materialise. In support of his submission, the learned counsel has placed reliance on a judgement of the Supreme Court in the case of Rajendra and ors. v. State of Rajasthan and ors., (1999) 2 SCC 317 : 1999(3) SCT 294 (SC) and argued that in cases where there is paucity of funds resulting into abolition of posts it has been held that no mandamus could be issued. The learned counsel has also argued that merely because there is a clause in the advertisement that the post was likely to continue the incumbent to a temporary post co-terminus with the project would not acquire any additional right. He has also placed reliance on another judgment of the Supreme Court in the case of K. Shekar v. V. Indiramma and ors., 2002(2) RSJ 165 : 2002(2) SCT 381 (SC).  Findings :  20. Before adverting to the controversy on merit, it would be appropriate to clear a doubt with regard to maintainability of the writ petition which has arisen on 10.9.2003 resulting into placing on record a copy of memorandum of association and rules leading to the establishment of Regional Engineering College, Kurukshetra (respondent No. 4). A similar controversy had arisen in respect of the Regional Engineering College, Sri Nagar before the Supreme Court in the case of Ajay Hasia (supra). According to the judgment in Ajay Hasia's case (supra) there are 15 Engineering Colleges in the country sponsored by Government of India. The Regional Engineering College, Kurukshetra (respondent No. 4) is one of them. After detailed examination, the Supreme Court has found in paragraph 15 of the judgment that a writ would be maintainable against a Regional Engineering College because the memorandum of association and the rules of the Society showed that the composition of the Society is dominated by the representatives appointed by the Central Government and the State Governments with the approval of the Central Government. The finances required for running the College were provided entirely by the Central Government and the Government of Jammu & Kashmir. The rules made by the Society were required to have the prior approval of the State Government and the Central Government. The accounts of the Society have to be submitted to both the Central Government as well as the State Government for their scrutiny and satisfaction. Therefore, it has been found that the control of the State and the Central Government is all pervasive and the College will have to be amenable to writ jurisdiction.  21. Now the first question which requires determination by this Court is as to whether respondent No. 4 is under an obligation to merge the ED Cell with the College. A perusal of Annexure R-1 containing general information and guide- lines on the establishment of Enterpreneurship and Development Cell in Education Institution shows that the ED Cells were established by the Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India to utilize the potential expertise and enthusiasm which has been shown in the field of Enterpreneurship Development by the Technical institutions so that sufficient infrastructure facilities be created which may require to promote the activities of the NSTEDB on regional basis. To start with financial support was provided by the Department of Science and Technology on yearly basis and thereafter the financial responsibility was to shift on the Regional Engineering Colleges for running the ED Cells and to absorb the members of the Faculty/staff in the main stream of the College/University after the period for financial assistance has expired. Accordingly, the ED Cell was established and on the basis of advertisement, the petitioner was appointed on the post of Senior Project Leader on 9.8.1989 vide Annexure P.2. He discharged his duties to the entire satisfaction of the respondents and the Board of Directors in its meeting held on 23.2.1991 changed its name to Industrial Liaison and Technical Development and the name to the post of Senior Project Leader was re- designated as Assistant Professor. It is appropriate to mention that a certificate/affidavit in the form of Appendix A has been furnished by respondent No. 4 undertaking that after the financial assistance from the Department of Science of Technology, Government of India was stopped, the faculty members of the ED Cell along with the staff were to be adjusted in the Institution/College to become part of the main stream. In this regard the College Advisory Committee on ED Cell submitted a report. The committee was comprised of Dr. S.K. Sharma, Chairman and Professor-in-charge of ED Cell, Dr. S.K. Chakarvarti, Member, Professor-in-charge, Academic Affairs, REC, Kurukshetra and Shri R.K. Arora, Member, Deputy Registrar (Accounts), REC Kurukshetra. In report Annexure P.12, it has been specifically mentioned that a mandatory undertaking has been given by the Regional Engineering College, Kurukshetra (respondent No. 4) that ED Cell was to merge into main stream of the institution for running on a continuous basis. The undertaking furnished by respondent No. 4 has been duly acknowledged by the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India. The aforementioned report would itself prove that the ED Cell was required to be merged with the main stream and even the Advisory Committee had made recommendations to that effect. The two paras report of the Advisory Committee reads as under :-  "Background Enterpreneurship Development Cell at Regional Engineering College, Kurukshetra was established along with other RECs in accordance with the guide-lines issued by DST on "Establishment of Enterpreneurship Development Cells in Educational Institutions" published in Nov. 1986. According to these guide- lines, DST provides financial support on a yearly basis for 3 to 5 years. Afterwards, the Parent Institute takes responsibility to continue the Cell. Accordingly, EDC merger into normal stream of the Institution for running on a continuing basis. To this effect, a mandatory undertaking has been given by our Institute which has been acknowledged by DST vide their letter No. 11/3/89 (NEB) Vol. V dated 17.9.99. Request for merger of EDC with the Host Institution has been received from DST vide their letter No. 11/3/89(NEB) Vol. V dated 17.9.99. DST has regulated the financial assistance of our EDC @ 75% during 2000-2001 and @ 50% during 2001- 02. The financial assistance by DST will continue only till March 31, 2002. Recommendations In the light of mandatory directive by DST and the undertaking given by the College, it is recommended that the EDC be merged with the Institution under the defined terms and conditions." 22. It is further appropriate to mention that even the Ministry of Science and Technology, Government of India vide communication Annexure P.13 had made it clear to respondent No. 4 that the financial assistance to the ED Cell would be available upto 31.3.2002 and necessary steps were to be taken by respondent No. 4 to ensure the continuation of ED Cell after that period. It is further pertinent to mention that in the advertisement Annexure P.1, it was specifically mentioned that the post on which the petitioner was appointed was temporary but the same was likely to continue. From a perusal of the documents mentioned hereinabove, it becomes evident that there is an obligation on respondent No. 4 to absorb the faculty members and other staff of ED Cell. Respondent No. 4 had given an undertaking in the form of Appendix "A" which is to the effect that after financial assistance by the Department of Science and Technology, Government of India was over then the staff and the faculty members were to be adjusted in the Regional Engineering College, respondent. It is evident that for over 12 years respondent No. 4 enjoyed financial assistance. Once respondent No. 4 has taken benefit of an undertaking it is impermissible to shun its responsibility. It cannot approbate and reprobate. It is infact estopped to go back from its obligation.  23. Another related aspect which requires determination is whether the Board of Governors was apprised with correct facts leading to the passing of resolution on item No. 94.26 declining to merge the ED Cell with the College. The answer to this question would be dependent on the analysis of various documents placed on record by the parties. The agenda item No. 94.26 (Annexure P.11 continued) or Annexure R-4/3) has indicated that the ED Cell required (i) Chief Project Coordinator (ii) Sr. Project Leader (iii) Jr. Stenographer (iv) Peon. It reveals that Shri R.K. Singal had worked as Chief Project Coordinator and joined on 1.8.1989 but lateron left the College. On 16.2.1990, the petitioner is stated to have joined as Senior Project Leader of ED Cell in the pre-revised scale of Rs. 3700-5700/- who was continuing as Incharge of the ED Cell. However, misstatement occurred when it was stated that two posts of Junior Stenographer and Peon were never filled up. As a matter of fact, one Shri Prem Kumar was appointed vide Annexure P.14 on 15.9.1989 as Steno-typist but later on he was appointed as such in the College vide Annexure P.15 on 1.2.1991. Similarly, Smt. Shashi Bala was appointed as Steno-typist in the ED Cell on 7.8.1995 vide Annexure P.16 and Shri Devinder Singh was appointed as Junior Scale Stenographer on 11.4.1997 vide Annexure P.17 and granted extension vide Annexure P.18. Shri Devinder Singh, however, was transferred from the ED Cell to the Principal's office on 5.12.2000 vide Annexure P.19. The detailed averments have been made in paragraph 18(a), (b) and (c) of the writ petition with regard to appointment of Shri Prem Kumar, Smt. Shashi Bala and Shri Devinder Singh. In the corresponding para of the written statement filed by respondent No. 4, it has been stated that after appointment in the ED Cell, Shri Prem Kumar had applied against an advertised post by respondent No. 4 and he was selected. About Smt. Shashi Bala it has been stated that she was holding the substantive post of Clerk with respondent No. 4-College and was simply posted to cope with the administrative work of ED Cell. She was repatriated to the College lateron. The stand with regard to Shri Devinder Singh is that on 24.12.1998, he was selected for the post of Clerk in the College and he joined as such on 24.12.1998.  It is thus evident that the Board of Governors was wrongly informed that the two posts, namely, Junior Scale Stenographer or Peon were never filled up. The posts were filled up at one time by appointment of Shri Prem Kumar and at another time Shri Devinder Singh was appointed.  24. I am further of the view that once the pay scale of Rs. 3700-5700/- has been revised to Rs. 12000-18300/- w.e.f. 1.1.1996 and the same scale has been given to the Assistant Professors working in the College w.e.f. 1.12.1999, then there was no reason for denying the same pay scale to the petitioner. The Board of Directors in its meeting held on 23.2.1991 has redesignated the post of Sr. Project Leader as Assistant Professor. In other words there was equation. It may be true that the afore-mentioned recommendations were not implemented but the post was declared equivalent to that of Assistant Professor. That itself is sufficient to conclude that the petitioner is entitled to the pay scale of Assistant Professor. This view is fully supported by a judgement of this Court in the case of Dr. Sukhdev Singh v. State of Punjab, 1991(2) SLR 336 : 1991(2) SCT 209 (P&H) and a judgment of the Supreme Court in the case of Employees of Tannery and Footwear Corporation of India v. UOI, 1991(2) SLR 131 : 1991(2) SCT 339 (SC). In fact an impression has been created that after filing of Civil Writ Petition No. 15371 of 2000, seeking payment of revised pay scale, respondent No. 5 Shri N.P.Mehta who is Principal of the College has taken many steps which led to the filing of second petition, namely, Civil Writ Petition No. 4579 of 2002. It is appropriate to mention that notice of motion was issued in the first petition on 11.1.2001. Various steps which respondent No. 4, the Principal of the College has taken against the petitioner have already been detailed in the preceding paras of this judgment. As a consequence, the petitioner suffered heart disease in August, 2001 and underwent open heart by-pass surgery on 28.9.2001. His medical bills were not reimbursed nor his salary was paid. However, he received his salary from July to October, 2001 on 13.11.2001. The petitioner appears to have passed through very hard time. At this juncture, I am reminded of a judgment of the Supreme Court in P.K. Ramachandra Iyer and others v. Union of India, 1983(3) SLR 495. In that case, the benefit of the revised pay scale was not granted to the incumbent already working on the post of by drafting some additional qualification which was found to be wholly irrational. The posts of Professor of Animal Pathology, Animal Genetics and Veterinary Parasitology were advertised to fill up by direct recruitment. The Supreme Court allowed the writ petition and noticed in paragraph 16 of the judgment the domestic atmosphere at the Indian Council of Agricultural Research and suicide committed by the Agriculture Scientists. The observations of their Lordships read as under :-  "........Unfortunately, since its inception, the domestic atmosphere has not proved congenial to the flowering of the genius of the country's best talent in agricultural research. This came to light when on May 5, 1972, newspapers all over the country flashed the tragic news that a young agricultural scientists, Dr. V.H. Shah who was working as Senior Agronomist and Associate Projector Co-ordinator in the IVRI had committed suicide by hanging himself in his residence the previous night.
